name: Swan
description: Lifelong pair-bonding intelligence with sophisticated aerial coordination. V-formation flight reduces energy expenditure by 20-30% through vortex wake exploitation. Cygnets ride on parents' backs, learning navigation routes through direct embodied transmission. Territorial displays use synchronized head movements as conflict-resolution signaling, minimizing physical confrontation.

core_attributes.pattern: lifelong pair-bonding, V-formation energy optimization, cultural route transmission

scope.definition: Energetic savings for birds flying in V-formation relative to solo flight at equivalent speed — measured as reduction in heart rate (proxy for metabolic rate) for birds in trailing positions.

evidence.source: Weimerskirch et al. (2001) 'Energy saving in flight formation', Nature 413:697-698; Portugal et al. (2014) 'Upwash exploitation and downwash avoidance by flap phasing in ibis formation flight', Nature 505:399-402.
cross_domain_examples: great white pelicans in V-formation: 11.4% lower heart rate vs solo flight (Weimerskirch 2001)
northern bald ibis: wing tip positioning optimized to upwash within 0.5 cm — precise aerodynamic exploitation
competitive cycling drafting: 20-30% metabolic reduction for following rider — same wake energy recovery
fighter jet formation flight: induced drag reduction 15-20% in echelon — engineered analogue

scope.falsifiability: If heart rate monitoring shows no significant difference between V-formation trailing birds and solo flyers at same speed, the aerodynamic upwash explanation fails.
scope.measurement_limits: Savings depend on inter-bird spacing, formation geometry, and wingbeat synchronization. Precise positioning within 0.5-1 m is required — loose formations provide minimal benefit.

scope.definition: Synchronization of flight departure timing between monogamous swan pairs — correlation coefficient of departure decision between mated individuals vs random same-flock pairs.

evidence.source: Birkhead & Møller (1992) 'Sperm Competition in Birds', Academic Press; Devlin & Rosenfeld (2002) Bewick swan pair coordination studies.
cross_domain_examples: mute swan pairs depart within 2 s of each other vs 60-120 s for non-bonded pairs in same flock
whooper swan pairs remain together through 3+ migration routes despite 2000+ km annual travel
albatross pair bond: 10+ year partnerships with 0.96 breeding site fidelity — extreme pair bond persistence

scope.falsifiability: If departure timing correlation between mated pairs is statistically indistinguishable from random same-flock pairs across 100+ observed departures, pair bond does not provide coordination advantage.
scope.measurement_limits: Coordination is strongest in breeding season and migration. During post-breeding molt, pairs temporarily separate. Pair coordination efficiency decreases in large flocks where individual signals are masked.

scope.definition: Proportion of juvenile Bewick's swan migratory route accuracy that can be attributed to following experienced adults vs innate magnetic compass, determined by displacement experiments on first-year birds.

evidence.source: Rees (1987) 'Conflict of choice within pairs of Bewick's swans regarding their migratory movement', Animal Behaviour 35:1050-1059; Nolet & Drent (1998) migratory learning studies.
cross_domain_examples: juvenile swans displaced from family groups show 40% higher route deviation than family-accompanied birds
cultural route knowledge includes stopover sites not predictable from magnetic cues alone
whooping crane reintroduction via ultralight aircraft: demonstrates cultural route learning from surrogate parents

scope.falsifiability: If displaced first-year swans navigate to wintering grounds with equal accuracy as family-accompanied birds, cultural route transmission provides no navigational advantage beyond innate compass.
scope.measurement_limits: Family group disruption is ethically constrained, limiting experimental sample sizes. Cultural route learning may be most important for fine-scale stopover site knowledge rather than broad direction.
